page.layout: One printed page: running head and page number at top; one text column with a marginal reference in the left margin ("p. 26 l. 21."); a small signature mark at the bottom right.

main_text.p: rationem, regessisse ان كنت صادقا فلا اصلح للقضاء s, وان كنت كاذبا فالكاذب لا يصلح للقضاء verax sim, non sum ei idoneus, sin mendax, non est mendax aptus judicis officio exequendo. Alcoranum, eo quo mortuus est loco, perlegisse fertur septies milliies. Socii Maleci & Shafeienfis, & Hanbali vocantur apud Shareftaninm اصحاب الحديث, Dictorum Mohammedis retinentes, funtque praecipuè Hejazenses, at asseclæ Abu Hanifa اصحاب الرأي Rationi, seu sententiæ propriæ addicti, & sunt Eraci-enses.

p. 26 l. 21.Assonnah, i.e. Traditio الحديث Ita cum reddimus eâ notione quâ eæ doctrinæ Iudaicæ partes quæ תורה שבעל פה seu legem ore tenus traditam (ut loquuntur) constituunt, & quæcunque in lege Mosis expressa non reperiuntur, Traditiones audiunt. Ita scil. continet Assonnah apud Mohammedistas, quicquid Mohammedis dicto vel facto præeuntis, magis quam ipsius Alcorani, authoritate commendatur. Illud nos docet Ebnol Athir, his verbis quid sit السنة explicaturus الأصل فيها الطريقة والسيرة واذا اطلقت في الشرع فإنما يراد ما امر به النبي ونهى عنه وندب عليه قولا وفعلا مما لم ينطق به الكتاب العزيز ولهذا يقال في اصلاح الشرع الكتاب والسنة اي القران والحديث Radix seu primaria hujus vocis significatio, est via & conversatio [ seu vitæ institutum ]

page.notes: Marginal reference "p. 26 l. 21." is beside the paragraph beginning "Assonnah". A small "s," in the Arabic line is probably a note mark, and I did not identify its referent. Arabic and Hebrew lines are copied from the scan and several words are uncertain; they are not checked against a source. The bottom-right mark is read as a signature "a 3" but is unclear. The bracketed "[ seu vitæ institutum ]" is printed in brackets.
